title: Formal Letter Writing
subject: english_grammar
syllabus_note: CBSE 2025-26 English Language and Literature (184) Section B Writing: a formal letter (complaint, enquiry, placing an order, or letter to the editor) in 100-120 words, 5 marks, one of two choices.

blocks.title: Five marks for one page
blocks.body:
In the board exam, a formal letter of about **100-120 words** carries **5 marks**. One mark is for **format** alone. Students lose easy marks by forgetting the date, writing 'Respected Sir' in the wrong place, or missing a subject line.

This chapter gives you a fixed format, model letters for every type in the syllabus, and plenty of practice so the format becomes automatic.

blocks.title: A letter that changed history
blocks.body: Gandhi wrote thousands of letters, to viceroys, newspapers and ordinary people. His letters were **polite, clear and firm**: he stated the problem, gave facts and asked for specific action. That is exactly what a good formal letter does.
blocks.future: Clear formal writing is needed for job applications, complaints to companies, emails to officials and letters to newspapers.

blocks.question: Why does a formal letter need a subject line?
options: It tells the reader the purpose at once, so the letter reaches the right action quickly
blocks.explanation: Busy officials read the subject first.

blocks.title: The CBSE formal letter
blocks.body:
**Types in the CBSE 2025-26 syllabus:** a **letter of complaint**, **letter of enquiry**, **letter placing an order** (and its reply, supply), and a **letter to the editor** on a social issue. You answer **one of two** choices, in about **100-120 words** (body), for **5 marks**.

**Layout:** use the **block format**: every line starts at the left margin; leave a line between parts.

**Marking:** format 1, organisation 1, content 1, accuracy 1, fluency 1.

**Language:** formal and polite. No contractions (*don't* → *do not*), no slang, no SMS language. Short, clear sentences. Use the names and addresses given in the question.

blocks.title: The eight parts of a formal letter
blocks.body:
| Part | Example | Tip |
|---|---|---|
| **1. Sender's address** | Examination Hall / 14, Shanti Nagar, Ahmedabad | Use the name and address given in the question; otherwise 'Examination Hall' |
| **2. Date** | 12 October 2026 | Write the month in words |
| **3. Receiver's address** | The Municipal Commissioner, Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation, Ahmedabad | Designation first, then office and city |
| **4. Subject** | Subject: Overflowing garbage bins in Shanti Nagar | One line, 6-10 words, tells the purpose |
| **5. Salutation** | Sir / Madam | Never 'Dear friend' or 'Respected sir' in an editor's letter |
| **6. Body** | three short paragraphs | (1) who you are and why you write; (2) details: problem, effects, facts; (3) request / action and thanks |
| **7. Complimentary close** | Yours faithfully | 'faithfully' to an unknown official |
| **8. Signature and name** | (signature) Rohan Mehta / Secretary, RWA | Use the name given in the question |

blocks.question: Which complimentary close is correct for a letter to a government official?
blocks.explanation: Use 'faithfully' when writing to an official you do not know personally.

blocks.question: Where does the subject line go?
options: after the receiver's address and before the salutation

blocks.title: Letter of complaint
blocks.body:
**Model letter of complaint (about 120 words, body)**

Examination Hall  
ABC Nagar, Ahmedabad

12 October 2026

The Municipal Commissioner  
Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation  
Ahmedabad

**Subject: Overflowing garbage bins in Shanti Nagar**

Sir

I am a resident of Shanti Nagar and wish to draw your attention to the overflowing garbage bins in our colony.

For the past three weeks the bins near the community park have not been cleared. Garbage is scattered on the road, stray animals tear the bags, and the foul smell has made walking unbearable. Mosquitoes are breeding, and several children have fallen ill with fever.

I request you to ensure that the bins are cleared daily and that more bins are placed in the area. I hope you will take prompt action.

Yours faithfully  
(signature)  
Rohan Mehta

blocks.title: Letter to the editor
blocks.body:
**Model letter to the editor (about 120 words, body)**

14, Lake View Society  
Vadodara

12 October 2026

The Editor  
The Times of India  
Vadodara

**Subject: Need to control noise pollution during festivals**

Sir

Through the columns of your esteemed newspaper, I wish to highlight the growing problem of noise pollution in our city during festivals.

Loudspeakers play at full volume till late at night, and firecrackers burst well beyond permitted hours. Students preparing for examinations cannot study, and elderly and sick people suffer greatly. Such noise can also damage hearing and cause stress.

The authorities should strictly enforce time limits and sound levels, and citizens must celebrate responsibly. I hope this letter will draw the attention of those concerned.

Yours truly  
(signature)  
Ananya Shah

blocks.title: Letter placing an order
blocks.body:
**Model letter placing an order (body)**

The Librarian of a school writes to a bookseller:

I am writing to place an order for the following books for our school library:

| S. No. | Title | Author / Publisher | Copies |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Wings of Fire | A. P. J. Abdul Kalam | 10 |
| 2 | The Story of My Experiments with Truth | M. K. Gandhi | 5 |
| 3 | Oxford Student's Dictionary | OUP | 15 |

Kindly send the books by 30 October 2026 and allow the usual discount for schools. Please ensure that the books are new and not damaged. Payment will be made by cheque on delivery.

blocks.title: How to plan the body in 2 minutes
blocks.body:
**Paragraph 1, purpose:** introduce yourself (if needed) and state why you are writing: *I wish to draw your attention to...*, *I am writing to enquire about...*, *I would like to place an order for...*, *Through the columns of your esteemed newspaper...*

**Paragraph 2, details:** facts, effects and examples: when, where, how long, who is affected, what has been tried. For an enquiry, list your questions; for an order, give a table with titles and quantities.

**Paragraph 3, action:** what you want done and by when; a polite closing line: *I hope you will take prompt action.*, *I look forward to an early reply.*

blocks.question: Which opening suits a letter to the editor?
options: Through the columns of your esteemed newspaper, I wish to highlight...
I am writing to order ten books.
blocks.explanation: Editors publish letters on public issues.

blocks.title: Useful formal expressions
blocks.body:
| Purpose | Expression |
|---|---|
| complaint | I wish to draw your attention to... / I regret to inform you that... |
| enquiry | I would be grateful if you could provide information about... |
| order | Kindly supply the following items at the earliest. |
| editor | Through the columns of your esteemed newspaper... |
| request | I request you to take immediate action. |
| closing | I hope you will look into the matter. / I look forward to your reply. |

**Avoid:** *Respected Sir* is acceptable to a principal, but use *Sir/Madam* for officials and editors in CBSE; never *Dear Editor friend*, *Thanking you* on its own line without a closing, emotional exaggeration, or very long paragraphs.

blocks.question: Which sentence is most suitable in a formal letter?
options: I would be grateful if you could look into the matter.
blocks.explanation: Formal letters are polite and clear.

blocks.title: Memory tricks
blocks.body:
- **Order of parts: S-D-R-S-S-B-C-S: Sender, Date, Receiver, Subject, Salutation, Body, Close, Signature.**
- **Body = 3 Ps: Purpose, Particulars, Plea (request).**
- **To officials: 'Sir/Madam' ... 'Yours faithfully'.**

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.body:
1. Forgetting the **date** or the **subject**: you lose the format mark.
2. Writing **'Yours faithfully'** with a capital F or a comma error is minor, but writing **'Your faithfully'** is wrong.
3. Inventing your own name when the question gives one: **use the given name**.
4. Writing 250 words: stay within **100-120 words** in the body.
5. Using contractions and slang.

blocks.title: Try this in class
blocks.body: Give students a jumbled letter (eight parts on cards). In pairs, they arrange them in order in one minute, then write the body for a given situation.

blocks.title: Think and explain
blocks.body: Which problem in your area deserves a letter to the editor? Plan the three paragraphs.

blocks.title: Where this leads
blocks.body:
- **Analytical Paragraph:** the other writing task in the paper.
- **Real life:** job applications, complaints to companies, emails to schools and offices.

blocks.title: Mastery challenge
blocks.body:
You are Kavya / Kunal of 22, Green Park, Surat. Write a letter to the Station House Officer complaining about frequent chain-snatching in your area. (100-120 words)

**Model answer (outline):** Sender's address and date; The Station House Officer, Adajan Police Station, Surat; Subject: Frequent chain-snatching in Green Park; Sir. Para 1: resident of Green Park, writing to report rising chain-snatching. Para 2: four incidents in two weeks near the market road in the evening; women afraid to walk; poor street lighting. Para 3: request regular police patrolling, CCTV cameras and better lighting; hope for prompt action. Yours faithfully, signature, Kavya.

blocks.title: Chapter summary
blocks.body:
- Formal letters: complaint, enquiry, order/supply, letter to the editor; 100-120 words; 5 marks.
- Eight parts in block format; subject before salutation; 'Yours faithfully' to officials.
- Body in three paragraphs: purpose, details, request.
- Formal, polite, clear language; use the given names.

blocks.title: Exam tips
blocks.body:
- Write the format first, then the body: it secures the format mark.
- Underline the key words in the question (who writes, to whom, about what).
- Count roughly 10-12 lines of body; do not exceed the limit.

blocks.front: What are the eight parts of a formal letter?
blocks.back: Sender's address, date, receiver's address, subject, salutation, body, complimentary close, signature and name.

blocks.front: How should the body be organised?
blocks.back: Three paragraphs: purpose, details (facts and effects), request or action with a polite close.

blocks.front: Which close is used for officials and editors?
blocks.back: Yours faithfully (or Yours truly for an editor).
